ai.seen: Explanation of a text preview rendering fix and status of continuous integration.
ai.title: Text preview layout fix

body:
I fixed the text preview for real this time: the off-white or gray paper now fills the whole box, with the text centered on it. It’s on main. Since CI is off, the fix hasn’t been compiled or tested anywhere yet; you’ll be the first to see it after Update Margin. If the update fails, Margin keeps your current version and shows the error.

What was wrong: the text picture is saved at double resolution, but the drawing code only filled a quarter of it. That left the text in the bottom-left corner and the rest of the box empty. This bug was older than my change last round, which is why that change made no visible difference.

Your existing text captures: they still have the broken picture, so Margin redraws them once the first time it launches after the update. It runs in the background and takes a moment.

What “CI” is: I think the “Cl” you saw is CI, short for continuous integration. It’s a GitHub service that builds and checks the app in the cloud whenever I push. For Margin it rents a Mac each time and:

builds the app,
runs about 130 automated tests,
makes one real call each to Gemini and OpenAI to confirm the keys work,
compiles the app icon file for Macs that can’t do that themselves.

Do we need it? Not to use Margin. Update Margin builds the app on each person’s Mac, which is why your friends could pull without it. What you lose without CI:

No safety check: I can’t confirm a change builds before you get it. A mistake would first show up as a failed Update Margin on your Mac, though your current version keeps working.
No icon refresh: the icon file only needs recompiling if we change the icon again.

Why the limit hit: builds on GitHub’s Macs are expensive for private repos. GitHub counts each Mac minute as ten regular minutes. I’ve also been triggering two builds per change, one per branch.

What I’d do: run CI only for main and only when app code changes, which roughly halves the usage. Then raise the spending limit a little before the deadline if you want the checks back. Or we skip CI until Monday and I’m extra careful. Which do you prefer?

rationale: keeping claude's explanation. the why of a fix matters too
title: Why text previews were broken

ai.seen: A list of HCI concepts behind clustering captures.
ai.title: HCI terms for sensemaking

body:
Sensemaking: collect, organize, find patterns, build a story (Pirolli and Card).
Spatial hypertext: meaning comes from where things sit, not from folders.
Incremental formalization: people resist structure early, so let it emerge.
Mixed-initiative interface: the AI suggests and the human decides.
rationale: words for what our board already said. clusters emerge, folders are imposed
title: Sense-making, in HCI terms

alternatives: Only a timeline. Let AI write the themes and the story.
body: The timeline keeps the process as it happened. The cluster is where you get messy: drag captures between groups, make new ones, rename them. Margin makes the first grouping, the rest is yours.
rationale: timeline = what happened. cluster = where you get messy
title: Two views: timeline and cluster
